issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 5 asserts that for any given $\varepsilon \in (0, \nu)$ and $c > 1$, there exist $T_{\mathrm{update}} > 0$ and $h_0 > 0$ such that $V(x_k) \leq \varepsilon$ for all $k$ and all $h \in (0, h_0)$. In the proof, the Hessian variation across the block of $n = \lceil T_{\mathrm{update}}/h \rceil$ steps is bounded by $(T_{\mathrm{update}}/h + 1) \frac{\Gamma \overline{C}}{c H_{\min}} \tilde{\varepsilon}^q$ in (31). For any fixed $T_{\mathrm{update}} > 0$ and fixed $\tilde{\varepsilon} > 0$, this bound diverges to $+\infty$ as $h \rightarrow 0^+$, so it cannot be bounded uniformly for all $h \in (0, h_0)$. The proof attempts to circumvent this by fixing $h = \frac{1}{2} h_0(\tilde{\varepsilon})$ and asserting that for smaller $h$, 'one can further shrink $\varepsilon'$ to maintain the inequality.' This reverses quantifiers by making the candidate invariant sublevel set $\varepsilon'$ depend on $h$ (with $\varepsilon'(h) \rightarrow 0$ as $h \rightarrow 0$), which invalidates the induction argument across subsequent update blocks and fails to prove that any fixed sublevel set $V^{-1}([0, \varepsilon])$ is invariant for all $h \in (0, h_0)$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must provide an argument controlling the cumulative drift of the Hessian over $n = \lceil T_{\mathrm{update}}/h \rceil$ steps that does not diverge as $h \to 0$, or restrict the update period to depend on step size such as $n = O(1)$.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 5 is invalid as stated and proven; the theoretical guarantee of positive invariance under Algorithm 2 for any fixed time update period $T_{\mathrm{update}}$ independent of step size $h$ is unestablished.
issues.title: Invalid quantifier reasoning and divergent bound in proof of Theorem 5
issues.why_classification: Theorem 5 is one of the main theoretical contributions of the paper, intended to validate the practical periodic adaptive gain algorithm (Algorithm 2). Because the proof's bound diverges as $h \to 0^+$ and relies on circular quantifier reversal, the primary claim fails and cannot be repaired within the existing architecture without altering the guarantee or algorithm assumptions.
